title: Reduced rational homology of the proper interval in a product of finite chains
statement: Let $r\geq1$ and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbf N^r$ be nonzero. Order $[0,m]=\prod_{i=1}^r\{0,\ldots,m_i\}$ coordinatewise, and let $T_m=[0,m]\setminus\{0,m\}$. Define an augmented chain complex $A(m)$ of rational vector spaces [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] as follows. For $k\geq0$, its basis consists of strict chains $v_0<\cdots<v_k$ in $T_m$; $A(m)_{-1}=\mathbf Q$ on the empty chain, and $A(m)_k=0$ for $k<-1$. The differential for $k\geq1$ deletes one vertex with signs $\sum_{a=0}^k(-1)^a[v_0<\cdots<\widehat v_a<\cdots<v_k]$; the degree-zero differential sends every vertex to $1\in\mathbf Q$, and the degree $-1$ differential is zero. If at least one $m_i\geq2$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for every integer $k$. If every $m_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $s=\#\{i:m_i=1\}$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for $k\ne s-2$ and $\dim_{\mathbf Q}H_{s-2}(A(m))=1$. This includes $s=1$, when $T_m$ is empty and the nonzero homology is in degree $-1$.
